## Colombo, 2024 · Growing iron into leafy greens

::: {.beat}
[January 2024]{.beat-when}

It started with a number: iron deficiency affects around two billion people, and it is rising in Sri Lanka. For my final-year research at BMS School of Science, studying for a Northumbria University degree, I asked whether two greens that Sri Lankan families already cook every week, mukunuwenna and kangkung, could be grown hydroponically to carry more iron.
:::

::: {.beat}
[February 2024]{.beat-when}

Stage one was propagation. I planted seeds and stem cuttings in 40 cocopeat-filled bags and 30 coconut-coir pellets, and watered them daily for four weeks.
:::

::: {.photo-grid}
![Coconut coir plugs ready for sowing](photos/1-colombo/2024-02-coconut-coir-plugs-ready-for-sowing.jpg){group="1-colombo"}

:::

::: {.beat}
[March 2024]{.beat-when}

After four weeks the plants moved into the two systems: the channels of a nutrient film technique (NFT) rig, and coconut-coir cultivation. Each system received three nutrient solutions, a control at 162.5 ppm iron and two enriched solutions at 200 and 250 ppm, with ten plants per group.
:::

::: {.photo-grid}
![Kangkung transplanted into the NFT channels](photos/1-colombo/2024-03-kangkung-transplanted-into-the-nft-channels.jpg){group="1-colombo"}

![Seedlings before transfer](photos/1-colombo/2024-03-seedlings-before-transfer.jpg){group="1-colombo"}

![The full NFT rig](photos/1-colombo/2024-03-the-full-nft-rig.jpg){group="1-colombo"}

:::

::: {.beat}
[April 2024]{.beat-when}

For five weeks I recorded the height and leaf count of every plant each week, changed the NFT solutions weekly and watered the coir system daily.
:::

::: {.photo-grid}
![Mukunuwenna and kangkung in full growth](photos/1-colombo/2024-04-mukunuwenna-and-kangkung-in-full-growth.jpg){group="1-colombo"}

![The NFT system on the rooftop](photos/1-colombo/2024-04-the-nft-system-on-the-rooftop.jpg){group="1-colombo"}

![Week four in the NFT system](photos/1-colombo/2024-04-week-four-in-the-nft-system.jpg){group="1-colombo"}

:::

::: {.beat}
[May 2024]{.beat-when}

At week five the plants were harvested and weighed. Samples went to an external laboratory for iron analysis by atomic absorption spectrophotometry, and the rest were dried at 40 °C for 48 hours, ground, and extracted in hot water. The first qualitative screens on the extracts followed.
:::

::: {.photo-grid}
![Harvested leaves packed in foil for drying](photos/1-colombo/2024-05-harvested-leaves-packed-in-foil-for-drying.jpg){group="1-colombo"}

![Qualitative screening of the extracts for polyphenols](photos/1-colombo/2024-05-qualitative-screening-of-the-extracts-for-polyphenols.jpg){group="1-colombo"}

:::

::: {.beat}
[June 2024]{.beat-when}

June was spent at the spectrophotometer: building standard curves and running five colorimetric assays for protein (Lowry), carbohydrate (phenol–sulfuric acid), phenolics (Folin–Ciocalteu), flavonoids (aluminium chloride) and antioxidant activity (DPPH).
:::

::: {.photo-grid}
![Building a standard curve for an assay](photos/1-colombo/2024-06-building-a-standard-curve-for-an-assay.jpg){group="1-colombo"}

![The Jenway spectrophotometer used for the colorimetric assays](photos/1-colombo/2024-06-the-jenway-spectrophotometer-used-for-the-colorimetric-assays.jpg){group="1-colombo"}

![Weighing samples on the analytical balance](photos/1-colombo/2024-06-weighing-samples-on-the-analytical-balance.jpg){group="1-colombo"}

:::

::: {.beat}
[July 2024]{.beat-when}

In July I completed the qualitative screening for tannins, polyphenols, terpenoids, steroids and anthraquinones, and analysed the results in SPSS with one-way ANOVA and post-hoc tests.
:::

::: {.photo-grid}
![Screening an extract for steroids](photos/1-colombo/2024-07-screening-an-extract-for-steroids.jpg){group="1-colombo"}

![Tannin test on a mukunuwenna extract](photos/1-colombo/2024-07-tannin-test-on-a-mukunuwenna-extract.jpg){group="1-colombo"}

:::

::: {.beat}
[August 2024]{.beat-when}

On 6 August 2024 I submitted the dissertation. It earned 84% and contributed to a First Class Honours degree, confirmed in November.
:::

::: {.beat}
[November 2024]{.beat-when}

In November I presented the work orally at ICIET 2024 at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura, and the abstract was published in the proceedings. [Read the full project](../projects/iron-biofortification/).
:::

## Dubai, 2025–2026 · From plants to pixels

::: {.beat}
[September 2025]{.beat-when}

In September 2025 I began an MSc in Bioinformatics at the University of Birmingham Dubai, on a 50% 125th Anniversary Scholarship. The goal: take the plant science I knew from the bench and learn to answer it with data.
:::

::: {.beat}
[November 2025]{.beat-when}

In November I went to the 3rd Healthy Longevity Symposium at Khalifa University in Abu Dhabi.
:::

::: {.photo-grid}
![At the 3rd healthy longevity symposium khalifa University abu dhabi](photos/2-dubai/2025-11-at-the-3rd-healthy-longevity-symposium-khalifa-university-abu-dhabi.jpg){group="2-dubai"}

:::

::: {.beat}
[December 2025]{.beat-when}

December brought the Genomics and NGS module, where the team project was to reproduce, or improve on, a published analysis. My work rebuilt a barley RNA-seq study on the university’s BlueBEAR supercomputer.
:::

::: {.photo-grid}
![Genomics and ngs team project brief reproduce or improve a published analysis](photos/2-dubai/2025-12-genomics-and-ngs-team-project-brief-reproduce-or-improve-a-published-analysis.jpg){group="2-dubai"}

![With my MSc cohort at the University of Birmingham Dubai](photos/2-dubai/2025-12-with-my-msc-cohort-at-the-university-of-birmingham-dubai.jpg){group="2-dubai"}

:::

::: {.beat}
[February 2026]{.beat-when}

From February to May 2026 I was a research intern at the University of Sharjah, analysing a public potato microarray dataset to see how roots respond to phosphate starvation. That month I also visited WHX Labs Dubai. [The internship project](../projects/potato-phosphate/).
:::

::: {.photo-grid}
![Visiting whx labs Dubai](photos/2-dubai/2026-02-visiting-whx-labs-dubai.jpg){group="2-dubai"}

:::

::: {.beat}
[May 2026]{.beat-when}

By May I had finished the taught modules with an 81% average and was deep into my MSc research: could drone images of more than 250 potato varieties reveal late blight?
:::

::: {.photo-grid}
![What the drone saw potato canopy from above](photos/2-dubai/2026-05-what-the-drone-saw-potato-canopy-from-above.jpg){group="2-dubai"}

:::

::: {.beat}
[July 2026]{.beat-when}

In July my team of three took first place in the Abiomix rare-disease challenge at the BioConnect 2026 sprint, and the project went on to the BioConnect Accelerator. [The project](../projects/rare-disease-reanalysis/).
:::

::: {.photo-grid}
![Our team presenting re analysing the unsolved at bioconnect 2026](photos/2-dubai/2026-07-our-team-presenting-re-analysing-the-unsolved-at-bioconnect-2026.jpg){group="2-dubai"}

![Receiving first place at bioconnect 2026](photos/2-dubai/2026-07-receiving-first-place-at-bioconnect-2026.jpg){group="2-dubai"}

![With fellow participants and mentors at bioconnect 2026](photos/2-dubai/2026-07-with-fellow-participants-and-mentors-at-bioconnect-2026.jpg){group="2-dubai"}

:::

::: {.beat}
[September 2026]{.beat-when}

In September I defended my thesis, and the next day our rare-disease work was shown as a poster at the UAE Rare Disease Society Congress. [The thesis](../projects/potato-late-blight/).
:::
